sections.content:
Irony in Spanish rarely announces itself. Two of its sharpest everyday tools are **understatement** (saying far less than the facts justify) and **overstatement** (inflating a minor fact until the contrast makes the listener smile).

Common **understatements** include *no está mal* ("not bad at all"—often high praise, or dry irony when paired with an extreme figure), and *un poquito* ("a tiny bit" used for a huge excess: *Llegaste un poquito tarde: solo dos horas*). In both cases, the gap between the modest wording and the real scale carries the humour.

Common **overstatements** and framing chunks include *nada menos que* ("no less than", often highlighting an absurdly large or ironically small number), *para colmo* ("to top it all off"), and calling an ordinary chore *una hazaña* ("a feat"). When someone misses the irony, speakers clarify with *lo digo en broma* ("I'm only joking") or point out *la exageración*.

sections.title: Understatement vs overstatement in speech
rows: *no está mal* (understated praise or dry irony)
*Sacó un diez en el examen: no está mal.* (She got top marks: not bad at all.)
*El informe es un poquito largo: tiene cien páginas.*
*nada menos que* (highlighting an impressive or absurd figure)
*Tardaron nada menos que tres horas en elegir una fecha.*
*Perdimos el tren y, para colmo, empezó a llover.*
*una hazaña* (ironic overstatement for a trivial act)
*Contestó el correo el mismo día: toda una hazaña.*

items.spanish: Llegaste un poquito tarde a la cena: empezamos hace hora y media.
items.english: You arrived a tiny bit late to dinner: we started an hour and a half ago.

items.spanish: Conseguimos entradas para la primera fila: no está mal, ¿verdad?
items.english: We got front-row tickets: not bad at all, right?

items.spanish: Necesitaron nada menos que cuatro reuniones para cambiar el título del archivo.
items.english: They needed no less than four meetings to change the file title.

items.spanish: Se fue la luz en la oficina y, para colmo, nadie había guardado el borrador.
items.english: The power went out in the office and, to top it all off, nobody had saved the draft.

sections.content: Watch the context: *un poquito* and *no está mal* are literal in neutral sentences (*Quiero un poquito de agua*). In writing, pair the understatement with a concrete detail (*solo dos horas*, *cien páginas*) so the reader spots the irony immediately.
